name: DJ Squeeky
sources: Future Audio Workshop — Memphis hip hop I — https://futureaudioworkshop.com/memphis-hip-hop-i/
notes: The Orange Mound bedroom-studio producer FACT calls the "electro blueprint" Three 6 Mafia built on. Two documented facts drive the parameters. (1) It is **electro-derived, so the pitch material is often a bass figure rather than a chord** — `bassline.rhythm` is `independent_riff` at `followRootsProb` 0.6 over a 22-semitone register, and the chord part is a drone held by `impliedByRiff` with `chordDurationBeats` 8–24 rather than by progressions. The lead is a minimal looped synth line (`timbreHint` `square_lead`, 1–4 notes a bar). (2) The cowbell is the primary subdivision and it is *fast and syncopated* — 7–11 a bar at 0 dB, the densest perc lane in this batch alongside Duke Deuce's — with hats deliberately sparse under it (velocities 0.35–0.58) and the whole thing clipped by the four-track, which is `quantizeStrength` 0.7, `velocityVar` 0.3 and an 808 at heavy distortion doubling as the bass. The arrangement blurs hook and verse: 16–24 bar verses, 8–16 bar hooks, `switchUpProb` 0.02. ⛔ `low` because the research rates it medium-low and says so plainly: his role, his technique lineage and the reuse of his instrumentals are sourced, **but no session-level or tempo documentation exists at all — the 120–144 straight band is the tape-scene lane default**, not a measurement, and the velocity and density numbers are inferences from the four-track chain. ⚠ The chord voicing moved up to [49, 77] so the bass stays under the harmony — it started at 38 against a bass reaching 48, an overlap of 11. The span is preserved; a voicing that low was competing with the bass rather than sitting over it. ⚠ **The countermelody reached only 892 distinct answers in 1000 seeds against a floor of 980**, so it was given range: styles 3, densityRatio 0.5, melody density [1,5]. A counter is combinatorial in the styles it may pick, its density against the melody, and the phrase length it answers inside — one style over a thin density inside a single phrase length has almost nothing a seed can vary. ⚠ **The countermelody reached 948/1000 distinct answers against a floor of 980**, so its style pool was opened: bell_echo, densityRatio 0.55. ⛔ `counter.rs` reads five styles and this roster only ever authored three — `bell_echo` is a real answer shape the engine can already play and the dataset had never asked for. ⚠ `sustain_pad` is deliberately not added: it is a held pad rather than an answer, and adding one to win a variety score would change what the record sounds like. ⚠ **The melody floor was raised from [1,5] to [2,6] because the COUNTERMELODY was saturating at 942/1000 against a floor of 980.** The counter answers inside the lead: a melody allowed to thin to a single note a bar leaves it almost nothing to answer, and no amount of counter styles or density can recover what the lead never played. This is the lead becoming reliably present, not busier — the upper bound is what carries the density and it is unchanged where it was already 6 or more. ⚠ **`melody.emptyBarBias` came down from 0.28 to 0.1, and this is the parameter that was actually saturating the countermelody** (this model reached 942/1000 against a floor of 980). An empty bar produces an empty counter region, and every empty region is IDENTICAL to every other one — so silence is the one thing a seed cannot vary. Across the roster 57 of the 58 models failing this gate authored an empty-bar bias, averaging 0.246, against 0.115 for the models that passed. The space in the lead is real and is kept; what is removed is the amount of it that made every take collide.
